full_judgment: 7. Leave was granted to consider the contentions that the judgment of the High Court Division is not a proper judgment of reversal inasmuch as the facts, circumstances and evidence considered and relied upon by the trial Court have not been considered and its reasonings have not been properly adverted to by the High Court Division in deciding the appeal before it and the High Court Division having relied upon certain extraneous facts and circumstances instead of considering relevant evidence on record on the question of defendant No. 2 being a bonafide purchaser of the suit property without notice of the plaintiffs' bainapatra its decision on the point cannot be legally sustained and, as such, the decree passed on appeal is liable to be set aside even if the first point as to genuineness of the bainapatra is held to have been correctly decided by it.
